implementationOptions:
**Option 1 — localStorage (RECOMMENDED).** A new `$lib/preferences/timeFormat.ts` module: a Writable store (or plain get/set pair) backed by `localStorage.getItem/setItem('mvox.time_format')` with values `'24h' | 'ampm'`, defaulting to `'24h'` when absent/invalid — mirrors `selectedCollectiveDbStore` (`src/lib/collectives/store.ts:20-22`) exactly. A new UI control on `/profile` (toolbar of 2 native buttons, same shape as `LanguageSelector.svelte`, NOT the `ProfileField`/tiered-visibility pattern) writes to it directly on click; no network call, no autosave queue, no `writesInFlight`/save-feedback states needed. The custom time control(s) built for sub-change A import the store/getter directly (module import, like `getLocale()`) to decide 12h-vs-24h rendering. **Satisfies:** rule 5 (preference exists and controls rendering), rule 4a is N/A (this isn't an in-situ text field, it's a new toggle, so the whole-field/Tab activation rule doesn't bind — though the control must still be a native, Tab-reachable `<button>`/`<select>` per rules 1/2). **Tests can assert (happy-dom):** store default value with empty localStorage; store round-trips a set value; clicking each option calls the persistence seam with the right value (inject a `setImpl` the way `LanguageSelector` does); the profile page renders the control both gated and ungated on collective (like `page.language-selector.spec.ts`); a mocked/injected time-format value is threaded into whatever component prop the custom time control exposes. **Cannot assert (happy-dom has no layout engine):** that a native `<input type="time">` actually paints 12h vs 24h in a real browser locale — that direction was already established as browser-only and needs a live smoke check (same category as the existing `[TRIGGER-24H-TIME]` review note and the project's 'live-click beats green unit tests' lesson).

**Option 2 — Entu `profile` entity property.** Add a third prop-def (`time_format`, string, `_sharing:'public'` to match the existing name/email cap per the T4.3 design doc §3.1) to the `profile` type, seeded via a new dated migration script (pattern: `scripts/migrations/t4-10-migrate-name-email-to-profile-2026-08-07.ts` for the POST shape). Read/write reuses the existing `listMyProfiles`/`resolveField`/autosave-queue machinery in `src/lib/profile/profileData.ts` + `profileEditQueue.ts`. **Problems this option must answer before it's viable:** (a) **multi-collective duplication** — `profile` entities are per-collective-db (`personId`/`db` are per-collective, confirmed via `auth.personIdByDb` in `src/lib/collectives/store.ts`), so a person belonging to N collectives would need the same value written N times, with no cross-collective sync — a genuinely worse UX than a single per-device value for what is purely a rendering preference, not sensitive/shared data; (b) it reopens the T4.3 NARROW-scope ruling (profile carries name+email ONLY, by explicit PO decision) and is exactly the kind of prop-def addition the CLAUDE.md schema rule flags as needing "a quick PO nod" even though additive props are cheap; (c) it requires the full save/autosave/tier UI (or a stripped-down variant of it) for a value that has no legitimate reason to be public/domain/private-tiered (a rendering preference isn't PII that needs visibility control) — `namePrivateDisabled`-style special-casing would have to be re-invented to suppress the irrelevant tier toolbar. **Tests can assert (happy-dom):** the same profileData/queue unit coverage the name/email fields already have (mocked entuFetch). **Cannot assert:** anything about which collective's profile "wins" when several exist with different values, because the product hasn't decided that (see openQuestions).
